feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. The controller is the iteration 4 controller unchanged, because the only gain test (iteration 1: kp 4.5, kd 0.3 on a 0.10 m track) scored lower at 53.7, and iteration 0 (kp 3.0, kd 0.2) and iteration 4 (same controller, 0.5 kg) are the best-scoring controllers. So any score change in this race is attributable to body_length alone. Iteration 4 (65.14) is the best result, and its failure is a single line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error 0.0666 and 0.0678 m. Iteration 3 (y 0.07 m) showed the forward offset does not remove that loss, and iteration 2 (16 mm footprints, wider span, 0.5 kg, 0.12 m body) scored lowest at 46.5, so larger footprints and wider coverage have not helped. Read the next race as follows. If line losses fall below 0.5 per run on the s-bend and slalom with max_error under 0.06 m, body_length (yaw inertia) is a real lever, and the next step is the smaller footprint test. If line losses stay at 1.0 per run with max_error still at or above 0.06 m, the yaw inertia floor is not the whole story, and the next step is mass. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, the robot is over-turning, and the geometry should move back toward the iteration 4 values.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay at 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom with max_error still at or above 0.06 m and steering_oscillation at or below 0.2, try mass 0.4 kg with body_length 0.12 m. Iteration 4 showed 0.5 kg raised the score to 65.14 (from 63.0 at 0.7 kg), so one more step down in mass is the next yaw-inertia test.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.2 with body_length 0.12 m, return body_length to 0.16 m and try wheel_track 0.14 m to slow the turn rate. Iteration 1 (narrow 0.10 m track with higher gain) scored 53.7, so faster turning alone has not helped.

If line_loss_events fall below 0.5 per run on the s-bend and slalom and the score exceeds 65.14, try sensor_size 0.008 m with the current sensor positions to sharpen the edge reading. Iteration 2 (16 mm footprints, wider span) scored lowest, so smaller footprints may help rather than hurt.
